supersedes: the all-covered-L3-in-supported-roster filter implemented by the R-stage supply review (v02_supply_review_summary.json), which misread DEFERRED (no quota) as DEFERRED (banned as intermediate step)

dag_eligibility: every intermediate family in SUPPORTED union DEFERRED
rule.machine_expression: anchor_family in SUPPORTED AND forall intermediate_family: intermediate_family in (SUPPORTED union DEFERRED) AND forall family: family not in OUT_OF_SCOPE
quota_credit: only a SUPPORTED anchor contributes family quota

rationale: The roster governs which families the benchmark actively covers (anchor + quota), not which real-workflow intermediate steps may appear. Rule B conflated the two semantics and dropped 21 of 52 DAGs -- including 15 of 22 merge topologies and 13 long chains -- because ordinary DEFERRED/OUT_OF_SCOPE steps (Repair Geometry, Erase, Extract by Location) poisoned whole DAGs. Rule A (anchor-only) restores supply but lets OUT_OF_SCOPE families re-enter as intermediate steps, erasing the capability boundary. Rule C keeps the boundary while restoring the supply.

known_counts_at_freeze.note: 37 is an intermediate statistic over the current candidate pool only; the 57 pending fan-out records and topology-taxonomy correction may change it; the authoritative count is recomputed after supply repair

topology_taxonomy_note: graph_profile classifies merge before branch: a DAG with both fan-in and fan-out is labeled multi_input_merge, masking its fan-out. The branch budget therefore needs an explicit semantics choice: 'primary-topology branch' (pure fan-out, no fan-in) vs 'contains branch structure' (pure + hybrid). Counts under both readings must be reported, never silently one of them.
